app.title: EmulSim — Double-Network Hydrogel Microsphere Simulator
app.summary: A person first picks a scientific mode and a polymer family. They then set the process recipe: hardware, stirring speed and time, phase volumes, polymer and surfactant concentrations, cooling, the crosslinker and its conditions. They enter target bead size, pore size and modulus, and keep each physical constant at its literature value or override it with a measured one. A run is blocked until input validation passes. It simulates the chain from emulsification through gelation and crosslinking to mechanical properties, and shows headline metrics against the targets, a plot per stage, objective deviations with suggested parameter changes (each linked to its derivation) and a trust verdict. Optional later modules simulate surface functionalisation steps and column or reactor performance using the fabricated beads.

task.text: Simulate a microsphere fabrication recipe end to end and judge how close the predicted beads come to target size, pore structure and stiffness, with guidance on which process parameter to change.

data.text: Process and formulation parameters plus material constants go in; the simulator produces per-stage results: a droplet size distribution, a 2D phase field of the gel, crosslinking kinetics over time, and mechanical curves and scalar properties. Measured calibration values can be loaded as JSON records.
data.item: one simulated fabrication run: a parameter set and its predicted bead properties

stage.text: designing a bead fabrication recipe in silico before wet-lab runs

mechanism.text: Input forms in two columns feed a validator that gates the run button. A finished run fills metric cards that show deviation from the targets, sub-tabs with one plot per pipeline level, and an assessment section that scores the objectives, lists suggested changes linked to derivation pages and gives a trust verdict. A scope selector adds downstream module tabs, and sidebar popovers load calibration data and set up uncertainty sampling.

field.text: multi-scale process simulation of emulsification and hydrogel microsphere fabrication in materials science

workflow.name: simulate a recipe against targets and get suggested parameter changes

steps.step: choose the model and the material system
steps.here: Sidebar Scientific Mode (Empirical / Hybrid / Mechanistic) and a Polymer Family selector that decides which formulation fields appear
Hardware mode, vessel and stirrer, RPM, emulsification time, phase volumes, polymer and surfactant concentrations, cooling rate, gelation model, crosslinker with concentration, temperature and time
Target modal or Sauter diameter, target pore size and target double-network modulus

steps.step: choose literature or measured values for constants
steps.here: Per-constant Literature/Custom toggle with a popover showing the matching calibration study; measured entries can also be uploaded as JSON or added by hand

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Validation blockers disable the run button. The run solves L1 PBE → L2 gelation → L3 crosslinking → L4 mechanics with a progress bar.

steps.step: compare the result to the target
steps.here: Metric cards show percent deviation from each target, and Dashboard/L1–L4 sub-tabs plot the size distribution, phase field, kinetics, Hertz contact and Kav curves
Three objective deviations are averaged into an excellent, moderate or poor match. Numbered suggestions link to derivation pages, and a trust verdict lists blockers and warnings.

distinctive: every result carries a model evidence tier, and a trust assessment says whether the run can be used for decisions
each physical constant can be swapped from a literature value to a measured one, with the wet-lab calibration study for it shown alongside
suggested changes link to pages deriving the required RPM, cooling rate or crosslinker dose by inverting the physics
pipeline scope can extend fabrication into surface functionalisation and chromatography or catalysis performance using the fabricated beads
